subject: Art & Design
source: National Curriculum (Art and Design). Drive Art & Design folder reviewed (Elements of Art deck, KS3 files) and the school's 'Art - Y9' lesson plan example used for format and the Y9 Zentangle topic.

lessons.title: The eight-pointed star: construction
objectives: Describe how geometry is used in Islamic art
Construct an eight-pointed star with ruler, protractor and compass

keywords.def: the mathematics of shapes, lines and angles
a light line used to build a design and later erased

starter: Bismillah. What is the radius of a circle?
How many degrees in a right angle?

teach.heading: Geometry in Islamic art
bullets: Artists used circles, squares and stars
Patterns repeat without end
Mathematics and beauty work together
teach.note: Show tiles and woodwork on screen. Say the tradition often avoids images of living things and focuses on geometry and calligraphy. Pupils need paper, pencil, ruler, compass, protractor, black pen, colours.

teach.heading: Step 1: circle and axes
bullets: Draw a circle with radius 6 cm
Draw horizontal and vertical diameters
Mark the centre
teach.note: Model slowly. Use very light pencil because these are construction lines.

teach.heading: Step 2: eight points
bullets: Use a protractor from the centre
Mark points every 45 degrees
This gives eight points on the circle
teach.note: Check: 360 divided by 8 is 45. Misconception: measuring from the edge instead of the centre.

teach.heading: Step 3: two squares
bullets: Join every second point
That makes the first square
Join the other four for a second square
teach.note: Show how the two squares overlap to form the star. Name it: eight-pointed star (octagram), often called khatam in design traditions.

teach.heading: Refine and outline
bullets: Rub out unneeded construction lines
Go over the star in black pen
Check every line meets a point
teach.note: Self-assess accuracy. Success criteria: points exact, lines straight, clean outline.

practice: How many degrees between eight equally spaced points on a circle?
independent: Draw a circle and mark eight points with a protractor.
Join the points to form two squares.
exit: Complete your eight-pointed star neatly in black pen.
Write two sentences explaining why geometry matters in Islamic design.
homework: How do you find the angle between eight points?
Which points do you join to make a square?
lessons.send: Practise the construction again at home with a different circle size.

lessons.title: Developing the star: layers, colour and repeat
objectives: Add inner lines to develop the star
Apply colour with a clear plan

keywords.def: to build on a design to make it richer
a clear difference, such as light against dark
to use a design again to cover a surface

starter: Describe the steps to construct the star.
How many sides has an octagon?
What is a complementary colour pair?

teach.heading: Look at your star
bullets: It has eight points
Inside is an octagon shape
Lines cross to make smaller shapes
teach.note: Pupils have their star from last lesson. Ask them to count the shapes inside.

teach.heading: Adding inner lines
bullets: Draw parallel lines inside each point
Make a band that weaves over and under
Erase gaps for the over-under effect
teach.note: Model one weave. Misconception: all lines should be solid; gaps show weaving.

teach.heading: Colour plan
bullets: Choose three or four colours
Use complementary colours for contrast
Keep matching shapes the same colour
teach.note: Show a plan on small thumbnail first. Link to Y6 colour wheel.

teach.heading: Repeating the star
bullets: Draw four stars touching at the tips
Look at the shapes between them
Fill the gaps with a new motif
teach.note: This shows how a design extends into a repeat. Pupils sketch only, do not need to finish.

teach.heading: Evaluate
bullets: What is working?
What would you change?
Give two targets
teach.note: Use a peer or teacher comment structure: what went well, even better if.

practice: Name the shape inside an eight-pointed star.
independent: Draw inner parallel lines on one point of your star.
Plan your colours in a thumbnail sketch.
exit: Colour your star using your plan and finish the weave effect.
Sketch four stars touching and design a filler shape.
homework: Why use contrast in a design?
What target will you set for your next design?
lessons.send: Find a pattern in a building or object at home and sketch its repeat.
